subject: business-studies
title: Margins & ARR Adventure
welcome_lead: Now you'll calculate margins as a % of revenue, work out ARR and judge investment decisions.
meta_desc: GCSE Business Studies — gross profit margin, net profit margin, average rate of return calculations.
final_note: You can calculate gross and net profit margins, and the average rate of return on an investment.

concepts.def: Money spent now to gain returns later
Profit from trading before interest and tax
How well a firm turns sales into profit

walkthroughs.body_html:
Margins show profit as a slice of revenue.

GPM = gross / revenue × 100. NPM = net / revenue × 100. Higher = more efficient at turning sales into profit.

ARR = (average annual profit ÷ initial investment) × 100.

It tells investors the % return per year. Compare ARR to interest rates and rival projects.

A rising revenue with falling margin means costs are growing faster than sales.

Investors and lenders watch margins to judge if a business is healthy and worth backing.

mcqs.q: Gross profit margin uses which formula?
options: (Net profit / costs) x 100
(Gross profit / revenue) x 100
(Revenue / costs) x 100
(Gross profit / total cost) x 100

mcqs.q: If revenue rises but net profit margin falls, the most likely cause is.
options: Costs are growing faster than sales
Higher savings
Lower competition
Fewer shareholders

mcqs.q: What is the difference between gross profit and net profit?
options: Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Gross profit and net profit are the same thing.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Gross profit = revenue minus cost of goods sold (direct costs only); net profit = revenue minus ALL costs including overheads, interest and tax. Net profit is the bottom line.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between profit and revenue?
options: Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
Gross profit is profit before VAT and net profit is profit after VAT.
Revenue is total income from sales (price x quantity sold); profit is revenue minus total costs — what is left after paying for everything.
Profit and revenue are different words for the same thing.

mcqs.q: Why can a profitable business still fail?
options: Because cash flow and profit are different — a business may be profitable on paper but run out of cash to pay bills, especially if customers owe money or stock ties up funds.
Profitable businesses fail only when employees steal.
If a business is profitable it cannot run out of money.
Profit is what businesses earn; revenue is what employees earn.
